h1:
Where to Stay in Phetchabun?
12 Hotels We Picked
from Real Reviews
heroSub: 12 Phetchabun hotels across every price level — sea-of-fog resorts on Khao Kho, clifftop glass houses on Phu Thap Boek, an in-town hotel with a pool, down to budget rooms from ฿600. Covering Khao Kho, Phu Thap Boek and the town center, from ฿600–2,490/night.
introH2: 🏙️ Why does choosing the right zone in Phetchabun matter?
introHtml: Phetchabun is a mountain province where the sights are spread far apart, and each zone gives a completely different feel — Khao Kho is the most popular sea-of-fog resort zone, packed with the Wat Phra That Pha Sorn Kaew temple, wind turbine fields and mountain-view cafes · Phu Thap Boek sits on the other side of the province (Lom Kao district), higher and colder, an open clifftop spot for chasing the fog · while the town center works best as a base before heading up — markets, temples, and stocking up before the climb · Many people book without thinking about which zone they'll explore, then spend hours driving up and down the mountain each day · This guide rounds up 12 Phetchabun hotels we picked across every level — from an English-village-themed resort on Khao Kho, to clifftop glass houses on Phu Thap Boek, down to in-town budget rooms from ฿600. Every one has real-review voices, a 3-site price comparison, and direct booking links.
mrtHtml: Phetchabun has no metro and almost no public transport on the mountains — your own car or a rental is by far the easiest way, especially for Khao Kho or Phu Thap Boek, since the mountain roads are steep and winding in places · Main zones in this guide: Khao Kho — Wat Phra That Pha Sorn Kaew, wind turbine fields, viewpoints, mountain-view cafes (about 1 hr drive from town) · Phu Thap Boek (Lom Kao district) — Pha Hua Sing cliff, viewpoints, cabbage fields, clifftop sea of fog (the final climb is steep) · Phetchabun town center — the clock tower, Wat Mahathat, markets and big-box stores, used as a base before the climb.

toc.name: Long Khao Camp Phu Thap Boek

entries.name: The Bluesky Resort @ Khao Kho
entries.revCount: 59 reviews · highest score in this list
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Khaem Son · Khao Kho · ~5–10 min to Wat Pha Sorn Kaew
entries.addr: 95 Moo 5, Khaem Son, Khao Kho, Phetchabun
entries.storyHtml: The highest score in this list at 9.4 — The Bluesky Resort is an English-village-themed resort set in a Khao Kho valley at around 800 m, where the air stays cool nearly year-round · The star is The Bluesky Garden, an English-style flower garden with a castle, a maze and a cafe that house guests enter free · Real reviews praise the European feel and waking up to a sea of fog at your door in winter, making it a fit for families and photo lovers who want to spend a whole day inside the resort.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Come November–January for both peak fog and peak blooms, wake before 7am to shoot the garden while it's quiet, and the resort is large — use the internal shuttle.
pros: The English-village look and flower garden are genuinely lovely for photos all day
Wake up to a sea of fog at your door in winter
Clean, nicely styled rooms with several zones to pick from
House guests enter The Bluesky Garden free
cons: Busy on long weekends and in winter — some photo spots have queues
Some room zones are far from the garden and restaurant; you'll need the shuttle

entries.name: Pino Latte Khaokho
entries.revCount: 100 reviews · cafe resort with fog views
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Khaem Son · Khao Kho · ~14 min drive to Wat Pha Sorn Kaew
entries.addr: 232 Moo 3, Khaem Son, Khao Kho, Phetchabun
entries.storyHtml: Pino Latte is a resort that started as a popular hilltop cafe, then grew into a fog-view stay, scoring 9.2 from 100 reviews · The draw is the upper Coffee Club terrace facing a panoramic mountain view — sip coffee while clouds drift to your balcony · There are both affordable hotel rooms and the upscale The Pino villas on the high ridge · Real reviews love the view and the spot near Wat Pha Sorn Kaew, but note that some hotel-zone rooms don't open onto the view as much as hoped — if you come for the view, pick the villa side.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If the budget allows, choose the upper-ridge The Pino villas for an open view and fog right off your balcony, and the kitchen closes early — plan dinner before dark.
pros: Panoramic mountain and fog views from the upper cafe terrace
On-site cafe and restaurant — lounge all day
The Pino villa rooms are spacious, clean, with full views
Near Wat Pha Sorn Kaew and Khao Kho's main sights
cons: Hotel-zone rooms are fairly small; some don't open onto the view
Kitchen closes early; limited menu after dark and no alcohol

entries.name: Hop Inn Phetchabun
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Samakkhi Chai Rd · town center · ~5 min to clock tower
entries.addr: 112/14 Samakkhi Chai Rd, Nai Mueang, Mueang Phetchabun
entries.storyHtml: Hop Inn is the most-reviewed hotel in this list with 979 reviews, a budget hotel in the town center scoring 9.2 and starting at just ฿600 · Reviews agree on clean rooms, comfortable beds, a wet-dry bathroom with strong hot water, and a big lot where you park right out front · The desk is open 24 hours, so late check-ins are no problem · It's an ideal first-night base in town before heading up to Khao Kho or Phu Thap Boek the next morning — just understand it's a place to sleep, with no pool or mountain view.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Touring Khao Kho–Phu Thap Boek, stay here the first night and climb in the morning to save money and avoid driving up in the dark, and fuel up and shop at the in-town stores before the climb.
pros: Clean rooms, comfy beds, strong hot water
Big parking right out front · 24-hr check-in
Central location near the clock tower, markets and big stores
Best value in the list, from just ฿600
cons: No breakfast (just free morning coffee); no pool or mountain view
Walls are fairly thin; some rooms have no window or face a wall

entries.name: Rom Karavek Khao Kho Resort
entries.revCount: 60 reviews · mixed-style houses on Khao Kho
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Khaem Son · Khao Kho · on a fog viewpoint
entries.addr: Khaem Son, Khao Kho District, Phetchabun
entries.storyHtml: Rom Karavek is a small boutique resort that builds its rooms as mixed-style houses spread across a viewpoint, scoring 9.0 · Loft houses with big glass walls, teak wooden houses, underground houses and farmhouses — every one faces the mountains and reservoir head-on · With only around 15 houses, the owner looks after guests personally · Real reviews rate the view and service especially high, with clouds drifting to your balcony at dawn. A great pick if you want a room with real character.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Want a wide balcony, pick the Farm House; love a photo angle, pick the glass Loft House — specify the room type when booking, and the open-air houses get insects, so bring repellent.
pros: Full sea-of-fog and mountain views; clouds at your balcony at dawn
Houses with real character — loft, wood and farmhouse
Lovely staff, close personal care, free snacks and drinks
Quiet and private, with an accessible starting price
cons: Some open-air houses get insects at night
Small property with limited shared facilities; the access road is steep in parts

entries.name: Blossom Hotel Phetchabun
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Nai Mueang · town center · ~840 m to market (walkable)
entries.addr: 9/19 Phetcharat Rd, Nai Mueang, Mueang Phetchabun
entries.storyHtml: Blossom Hotel is a small in-town boutique hotel that stands out for cleanliness, scoring 9.8 in that category on Booking.com for an overall 9.0 · What many reviews love is the new rooms, soft beds, plenty of pillows and power outlets, and a central spot just 840 m from the market — walk out for food · It has a spa, sauna, garden and terrace to unwind · Real reviews praise the cleanliness and the walkable location, making it a good in-town base before or after the Khao Kho–Phu Thap Boek climb.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Some rooms face the street, others the garden — ask for a garden-view room when booking if you want quiet, and there's no pool here, so look at SR Residence if you need one.
pros: Very clean — cleanliness scored 9.8; soft beds, plenty of outlets
Central location, walk to markets and restaurants
Spa, sauna, garden and terrace to relax in town
Attentive staff, breakfast to your room, free parking
cons: Small hotel with limited rooms; fills fast on long weekends
No swimming pool, and not a mountain-view resort on Khao Kho

entries.name: The Proud Resort @ Khao Kho
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Ban Kanok Ngam · Khao Kho · Rattanai reservoir view
entries.addr: 324 Moo 1, Ban Kanok Ngam, Khao Kho, Phetchabun
entries.storyHtml: The Proud Resort is set on a slope facing the Rattanai reservoir so nearly every room opens onto a sea of fog, scoring 8.7 · You can pick a private house for 2–6 guests or an air-conditioned VIP tent that gives a camp feel while still sleeping comfortably · Dinner is moo kratha / barbecue eaten together as a group, perfect for the cool air · Real reviews praise the view from each room and the quiet, the owner gets compliments for being friendly, and it holds a Tripadvisor Travelers' Choice — view and quiet over flashy facilities.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: When booking, ask which rooms face the Rattanai reservoir directly for the fullest view, and come October–February for peak fog. Bring warm clothes.
pros: The fog and Rattanai reservoir view from your room is as good as the photos
Air-conditioned VIP tents give a camp feel with comfortable sleep
Quiet, private atmosphere; a friendly owner
Moo kratha dinner suits the cool air, eaten together as a group
cons: Limited facilities; no swimming pool
Fog depends on the weather and isn't there every day

entries.name: Phuphamok Khao Kho Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Khao Kho · ~3 km from town · open high ridge
entries.storyHtml: Phuphamok is set on an open high ridge with a 360-degree view of fog and mountains all around, scoring 8.6 — something many Khao Kho stays can't match · It has houses of various sizes from a couples' cabin to a big house sleeping ten, plus a VIP camping ground for tent lovers · There's a cafe and a moo kratha spot where you grill while watching the sunset · Real reviews love the all-around view but note the food is more about the setting than the flavor.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: A big group should pick Ruen Phupha (sleeps ten) over booking several cabins, couples can take a smaller private cabin, and book moo kratha for the sunset.
pros: 360-degree fog and mountain view; fog around your cabin at dawn
Cabins sized from couples up to a group of ten
VIP camping ground on-site — for both cabin and tent lovers
Cafe and moo kratha with a good setting, grilling at sunset
cons: Food leans on atmosphere over flavor; the dipping sauce is sweet
Basic in-room amenities; some open-air cabins get insects

entries.name: Long Khao Camp Phu Thap Boek
entries.revCount: 220 reviews · glass houses by Pha Hua Sing cliff
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Pha Hua Sing · Phu Thap Boek · Lom Kao district
entries.addr: Ban Noen, Lom Kao, Phetchabun (Phu Thap Boek, Pha Hua Sing)
entries.storyHtml: Long Khao Camp is a camp/glass-house stay on Phu Thap Boek, set right by the Pha Hua Sing cliff with an unobstructed 180-degree sea-of-fog view, scoring 8.6 from 220 reviews · Options run from camping domes and glass houses to a glass-box unit with air-con and an outdoor hot-soaking tub · Real reviews say that in late rainy to early winter, fog drifts to your balcony almost every morning — soak in the tub while watching it. A much-talked-about fog-chasing stay on Phu Thap Boek, though you'll trade off some privacy and a steep climb.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For comfort and privacy, pick the glass-box unit with air-con and a tub (like Camp 7), and book only via the official site/page — there are several fake pages impersonating this name.
pros: Unobstructed 180-degree sea-of-fog view by the Pha Hua Sing cliff
Glass-house units have an outdoor hot-soaking tub facing the fog
Minimal, fresh-looking rooms with roomy usable space
Breakfast included, served as a box to your door
cons: Limited privacy in some units, and the climb is steep and narrow
Some units have no air-con and run on a generator; nights are very cold

entries.name: SR Residence Hotel
entries.revCount: 900 reviews · in-town hotel with a pool
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Sadiang · town · ~2 km from town center
entries.storyHtml: SR Residence is an in-town hotel with a pool that has plenty of reviews — 900 of them, scoring 8.5 · What reviews love is the new, clean rooms that are larger than expected for the price, an outdoor pool and kids' pool, a pool bar with live music, and many upper-floor rooms facing the rice fields with lovely sunsets · TripAdvisor ranks it #1 among B&Bs in Phetchabun · A good in-town base before the climb, though it's about 2 km from the town center, so you'll want a car.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For a rice-field and sunset view, ask for an upper-floor room facing the fields; for a quiet night, ask for one far from the pool and pool bar, since the live music runs late.
pros: New, clean, spacious rooms with fresh-looking furniture
Pool and kids' pool — good for families
Rice-field and mountain views with lovely sunsets upstairs
Tasty, affordable poolside restaurant; big free parking
cons: Live poolside music in the evening carries to nearby rooms
Away from the town center and main road; you'll need a car

entries.name: Khaokhotalamok Resort
entries.revCount: 120 reviews · Khao Kho fog, big groups
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Khao Kho subdistrict · Khao Kho · fog viewpoint
entries.addr: 53 Moo 3, Khao Kho subdistrict, Khao Kho, Phetchabun
entries.storyHtml: Khaokhotalamok is a large viewpoint resort built to handle big groups, scoring 8.4 from 120 reviews · Houses come in many sizes from a couples' cabin to a big house sleeping over a dozen, plus a camping ground, with a pool and an on-site restaurant · Real reviews rate the location and view high — step out your door on a winter morning to fog over the valley · But to be honest, room comfort is its lowest-scoring area; the strengths are the view, the space, and the value when you split a big house among many people.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for photos of your actual house and confirm the sleeping capacity before booking, since houses vary — pick an updated one that faces the view for the best value.
pros: Location and fog view score high; lovely winter-morning fog
Houses of many sizes let big groups and families stay together
Camping ground, pool and an on-site restaurant
Affordable starting price; great value split among a group
cons: Some houses look old and basic; standards vary house to house
Room comfort is the lowest-scoring area

entries.name: Station Phu Thap Buek Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Ban Noen · Phu Thap Boek · Lom Kao district
tags: 💰 Budget price on Phu Thap Boek
entries.addr: Ban Noen, Lom Kao, Phetchabun (Phu Thap Boek)
entries.storyHtml: Station Phu Thap Buek is a budget stay on Phu Thap Boek where every room faces a sea-of-fog view, scoring 8.2 from 432 reviews · The star is the open rooftop where you watch the sunrise and grill moo kratha while looking out at the fog · From just ฿900 you get to sleep on the mountain with a fog view — rare at this price · Real reviews rate the view and value high · Just understand it's a simple stay, not a resort, and nights up here are very cold.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask ahead about the moo kratha set and reserve a rooftop table for both evening and morning, and nights are genuinely cold — bring warm clothes and you can ask for extra blankets.
pros: Every room faces a sea-of-fog and mountain view
An open rooftop for lounging and grilling moo kratha with the view
Light starting price, great value for the view on Phu Thap Boek
Clean rooms, friendly staff, free parking
cons: A budget stay — decor and facilities are simple
Very cold nights; some rooms have no heater · drive the climb with care

entries.name: Khao Kho Overview Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Khaem Son · Khao Kho · ~5 rai grounds
entries.addr: 328-329 Moo 1, Ban Dong Long, Khaem Son, Khao Kho, Phetchabun
entries.storyHtml: Khao Kho Overview is a budget stay on wide ~5-rai grounds that delivers more than the price suggests, scoring 8.2 from just ฿990 · It has an outdoor mountain-view pool, an organic strawberry farm out back you can pick from in season, and rooms in many styles from loft houses and family rooms to forest domes and a vintage caravan · Real reviews love the wide space and the activities for kids, a fit for families and groups · Just note that some rooms vary in standard and the final stretch of access road is gravel.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Check breakfast directly with the property when booking, as platform info doesn't always match, and the final stretch is gravel — come in a car in good shape and drive slowly in the rain.
pros: Wide ~5-rai grounds with lovely mountain views to wander and shoot all day
Outdoor mountain-view pool and a strawberry farm to pick from
Many room styles — loft house, family room, dome and caravan
Affordable price; great value for families and groups
cons: Some rooms vary in standard; parts await refurbishment
The final stretch of access road is gravel, hard to drive in the rain

adviceTitle: How to pick the right Phetchabun hotel for your trip?

advice.head: On a tight budget, want the cheapest
advice.bodyHtml: → Hop Inn Phetchabun ฿600, a clean in-town budget hotel with easy parking · or Blossom Hotel ฿900, an in-town boutique with 9.8 cleanliness

advice.head: Want to wake up to fog on Khao Kho
advice.bodyHtml: → Rom Karavek ฿1,290, mixed-style houses with full views · or The Proud Resort ฿2,200, fog over the Rattanai reservoir at your door

advice.head: A photo lover after a special setting
advice.bodyHtml: → The Bluesky Resort ฿2,490, an English village with a flower garden and castle · or Pino Latte ฿1,900, a fog-view cafe resort

advice.head: Chasing clifftop fog on Phu Thap Boek
advice.bodyHtml: → Long Khao Camp ฿1,600, a 180° fog-view glass house with a soaking tub · or Station Phu Thap Buek ฿900, budget rooftop moo kratha with the fog

advice.head: Coming as a group or big family
advice.bodyHtml: → Khaokhotalamok Resort ฿1,400, a house sleeping over a dozen with a pool · or Phuphamok ฿1,700, a 10-guest house with a 360° fog view

advice.head: Want an in-town base before the climb
advice.bodyHtml: → SR Residence Hotel ฿1,100, new rooms with a pool · or Blossom Hotel ฿900, walkable to the market with a spa/sauna

advice.head: Family wanting a pool + kid activities
advice.bodyHtml: → Khao Kho Overview Resort ฿990, wide grounds, a pool and a strawberry farm · or SR Residence ฿1,100, a pool in town

noteHtml: 📌 Note: All prices are approximate and change with the date and season — always check live prices and compare the 3 sites before booking · In late rainy to early winter (Oct–Jan) the fog is at its best and stays on Khao Kho and Phu Thap Boek fill very fast; book 1–2 months ahead · Phetchabun is a mountain province with almost no public transport on the hills — your own car or a rental is easiest, and the mountain roads are steep and winding in parts · Some Phu Thap Boek stays must be booked via the official site/page only, so verify before transferring money · Article by ThailandAddict.com
faqTitle: FAQ — common traveller questions about Phetchabun hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which zone should I stay in within Phetchabun?
faq.a: It depends which zone you'll explore · Khao Kho suits sea-of-fog views, Wat Pha Sorn Kaew, wind turbine fields and mountain cafes (The Bluesky, Pino Latte, Rom Karavek, The Proud, Phuphamok, Khaokhotalamok, Khao Kho Overview) · Phu Thap Boek (Lom Kao district) is higher and colder, ideal for chasing clifftop fog (Long Khao Camp, Station Phu Thap Buek) · the town center works as a base before the climb, near markets and stores (Hop Inn, SR Residence, Blossom) · Khao Kho and Phu Thap Boek are on opposite sides and not a quick drive apart.

faq.q: ❓ How much do Phetchabun hotels cost?
faq.a: Prices vary widely: in-town budget rooms from around ฿600–900 per night · budget mountain/Phu Thap Boek stays around ฿900–1,600 · fog-view resorts and boutiques around ฿1,290–2,500 · big group houses and villas around ฿4,500–7,500 · In late rainy to early winter (Oct–Jan) and on long weekends, prices rise and rooms fill fast, especially on Khao Kho and Phu Thap Boek.

faq.q: ❓ Do I need a car in Phetchabun, and how essential is it?
faq.a: Fairly essential, especially for Khao Kho (about 1 hr from town) or Phu Thap Boek (about 1.5 hr, with a steep final climb), since there's almost no public transport on the hills · Renting or driving your own car is the most convenient and flexible · For some Phu Thap Boek spots, if you're unsure about the climb, you can use a local pickup truck to get up.

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should I book a Phetchabun hotel?
faq.a: For ordinary weekdays, 2–3 weeks ahead is enough · but in late rainy to early winter (October–January) when the fog is best, and on long weekends, stays on Khao Kho and Phu Thap Boek fill very fast — book 1–2 months or more ahead, especially good-view resorts and glass houses.

faq.q: ❓ Khao Kho or Phu Thap Boek — where should I stay?
faq.a: Khao Kho suits travellers who want a wide range of resorts, cafes, Wat Pha Sorn Kaew, and an easier climb — good for families and most visitors · Phu Thap Boek is higher and colder with denser, open clifftop fog, but a steep climb and camp-style stays — for serious fog-chasers · The two zones are on opposite sides of the province, so on a multi-day trip many people stay 1–2 nights on Khao Kho, then move to Phu Thap Boek for a night.

faq.q: ❓ Which site is cheapest for booking Phetchabun hotels?
faq.a: Prices on each site (Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com) differ by promotion, so always open all 3 to compare before booking — every review page here has full price-comparison links · For some camp-style Phu Thap Boek stays (like Long Khao Camp), book via the official site or page only, as fake pages impersonate the name; verify before you transfer money.
